title: The Dressmaker
about: A Paris-trained dressmaker comes home to the dusty Victorian town that ran her out as a child, and dresses it up for revenge.
cue: Pass the party pies when Tilly turns up to the footy final in red.

    Sandwiches and savouriesFooty final party pies with tomato sauceTilly's red dress at the footy final. Beef and black pepper pies, proper tomato sauce.How to make it500g beef mince1 brown onion, finely diced1 tbsp olive oil2 tbsp plain flour250ml beef stock2 tbsp tomato paste1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce1 tsp cracked black pepper3 sheets of shortcrust pastry2 sheets of puff pastry1 egg, beaten125ml tomato sauceBrown the onion and mince in the oil, breaking it up as it goes.Stir in the flour, then the stock, tomato paste, Worcestershire and pepper, and simmer until thick.Cool the filling, then line a greased 12-hole muffin tin with rounds of shortcrust.Fill, top with rounds of puff, press the edges and brush with egg.Bake at 200°C until puffed and deep golden, then serve hot with tomato sauce.Footballers dance asparagus rollsGertrude's dress for the footballers dance. Asparagus, lemon butter, soft white bread.How to make it2 bunches of asparagus, trimmed12 slices of soft white sandwich bread80g soft butter1 lemon, zested2 tbsp chives, finely chopped1/2 tsp cracked black pepperBlanch the asparagus in salted boiling water for 2 minutes, then plunge into iced water and pat dry.Beat the butter with the lemon zest, chives and pepper.Cut the crusts off the bread and roll each slice thin with a rolling pin.Spread with the butter, lay a spear across each slice, roll up tightly and cut in half.Pratt's counter sausage rolls with bush tomato chutneyWilliam's mum owes Pratt's 347 pounds. Pork and fennel, flaky pastry, bush tomato chutney.How to make it500g pork mince1 brown onion, grated1 carrot, grated40g fresh breadcrumbs1 tsp fennel seeds, crushed3 sheets of puff pastry1 egg, beaten1 tbsp sesame seeds125ml bush tomato or tomato chutneyMix the pork, onion, carrot, breadcrumbs, fennel and a good pinch of salt.Halve the pastry sheets, lay a log of filling along each and roll up, seam underneath.Brush with egg, scatter with sesame and cut into short lengths.Bake at 210°C until puffed and golden, then serve with the chutney.LuncheonSergeant Farrat's chicken a la king vol-au-ventsFarrat takes a feather boa as a bribe. Creamy chicken, mushrooms and tarragon in puff cases.How to make it600g chicken thigh fillets, diced40g butter200g button mushrooms, sliced1 red capsicum, diced2 tbsp plain flour250ml chicken stock200ml thickened cream1 tbsp tarragon, chopped8 large vol-au-vent cases1 cup frozen peasBrown the chicken in the butter, then lift it out.Cook the mushrooms and capsicum in the same pan until soft.Stir in the flour, then the stock and cream, and simmer until it coats a spoon.Return the chicken with the peas and tarragon and simmer until cooked through.Warm the cases at 180°C for 5 minutes, fill generously and serve.Wedding breakfast roast lamb with mint sauceGertrude marries William Beaumont. Garlic and rosemary leg, crisp spuds, fresh mint sauce.How to make it2kg lamb leg, bone in4 garlic cloves, sliced3 rosemary sprigs3 tbsp olive oil1.2kg floury potatoes, in chunks500g pumpkin, in wedges1 cup mint leaves, finely chopped3 tbsp caster sugar80ml malt vinegar80ml boiling waterStir the sugar into the boiling water, add the vinegar and mint and set the mint sauce aside.Cut small slits in the lamb, push in the garlic and rosemary, rub with oil and season well.Roast at 180°C for 1 hour 20 minutes for pink, adding the potatoes and pumpkin for the last hour.Rest the lamb for 20 minutes while the potatoes crisp up at 220°C.Carve and serve with the vegetables and mint sauce.From the cake trolleyMolly's chocolate brownies with wattleseed creamMolly's brownies for Irma's arthritis. Fudgy dark chocolate, wattleseed cream. Ours are plain.How to make it200g dark chocolate, chopped180g butter250g brown sugar3 eggs1 tsp vanilla extract100g plain flour30g cocoa powder300ml thickened cream2 tsp ground roasted wattleseed1 tbsp icing sugarMelt the chocolate and butter together over low heat, then cool a little.Whisk in the sugar, eggs and vanilla, then fold in the flour, cocoa and a pinch of salt.Pour into a lined 20cm tin and bake at 170°C until just set, with a fudgy middle.Whip the cream with the wattleseed and icing sugar and serve on the cooled brownies.Pots and cupsParis via Melbourne raspberry champagne cocktailTilly's train to Paris via Melbourne. Raspberry syrup, a sugar cube, cold sparkling.How to make it150g frozen raspberries75g caster sugar2 tbsp water4 sugar cubes1 bottle Australian sparkling wine, chilledSimmer the raspberries, sugar and water for 5 minutes, then push through a sieve and chill.Drop a sugar cube and a spoonful of syrup into each flute.Top slowly with the cold sparkling and serve.A pot of tea for the tableStrong enough to stand the spoon in.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
